[Regulations for Undergraduate Programme of Bachelor of Technology (Regulations 2019-I(A)), NSUT | Section: 9 GRADING | Clause: 9.6 | Page: 16]
Category: Grading System
Topic: F/FD/Ab count as fail and require re-registration
Applicability: B.Tech students (2019 onwards)

Rule Content:
9.6 Interpretation of the Grades a. Fail grade: A student obtaining Grade F/FD/Ab shall be considered as failed and shall be required to register for the course again. In case of the elective courses, if the student does not want to register again in an elective course in which he/she has failed (for EG, ED, EO, FE courses but not for CC or FC courses), then he/she can register afresh for a new elective course. However, grades F/FD, as applicable, shall be mentioned in the Grade Card even after passing the course. b. 'FD' grade: The FD grade indicates fail due to shortage of attendance in a course. c. 'W' grade: This refers to the withdrawal from the courses other than core courses. Withdrawal shall be allowed as per the guidelines issued from time to time by the Dean Academics. d. Audit/FE courses: For audit courses, grades shall be indicated however this will not be counted for the computation of the SGPA/CGPA.

Conditions: All courses
Exceptions: Electives (EG, ED, EO, FE) may be replaced by a new elective; not CC/FC

[Regulations for Undergraduate Programme of Bachelor of Technology (Regulations 2019-I(A)), NSUT | Section: 9 GRADING | Clause: 9.7 | Page: 16-17]
Category: Grading System
Topic: Rounding of SGPA/CGPA
Applicability: B.Tech students (2019 onwards)

Rule Content:
9.7 Computation of the SGPA and CGPA. a. The SGPA is the ratio of the sum of the product of the number of credits and the grade points scored in all the courses taken in a semester (including back-log courses), to the sum of the number of credits of all the courses taken by a student. b. The CGPA is also calculated in the same manner taking into account the best 162 credit courses of the student taken over all the semesters of a programme. c. The SGPA and CGPA shall be rounded off to 2 decimal points. d. CGPA shall be converted into percentage of marks by multiplying it with 10. Both CGPA and percentage shall be mentioned on the final transcript.

Conditions: SGPA and CGPA
Exceptions: None stated

[Guidelines for Mode of Registration for Student of Backlog Courses | Section: GUIDELINES FOR MODE OF REGISTRATION FOR STUDENT OF BACKLOG COURSES | Clause: Clause (a) | Page: 1]
Category: Backlog & Registration Modes
Topic: Backlog Course Registration Modes: Exam Only Mode (EoM) vs Study Mode (SM)
Applicability: Students with backlog courses who met attendance requirements originally

Rule Content:
(a) Students who had met the attendance requirements in the semester when the course was originally registered may choose one of the following modes: I. Exam Only Mode (EOM): In this mode, students can appear directly for the Mid-Semester Examination (MSE) and End Semester Examination (ESE) without being required to attend classes again. Their previously earned Continuous Assessment (CA) marks will be carried forward. Further, provided the date of the exam doesn't clash with their current semester exam. II. Study Mode (SM): In this mode, students must register for the backlog course in the same semester in which it is offered to their junior batch as part of the regular curriculum, or during the summer semester if the course is available. Attendance is mandatory, and students must meet the required attendance criteria to be eligible for the examinations.

Conditions: Exam Only Mode is permissible ONLY if the student met attendance requirements during original course registration, and exam dates do not clash with current semester exams. Previously earned CA carried forward.
Exceptions: unknown

1. Eligible students may apply for branch change at the end of the second semester (first year).
2. Academic criteria: Must have completed all course credits of 1st year in the very first attempt.
3. Minimum CGPA: Must secure CGPA >= 8.00 at the end of the 2nd semester (CGPA >= 7.50 for SC/ST category).
4. Allocation: Offered strictly on merit of CGPA against available sanctioned vacancy in the target branch.
5. Strength constraint: Branch change shall not exceed 10% of the sanctioned intake of any branch, and branch strength cannot fall below 85% of sanctioned strength.
6. Once branch change is allocated and notified, it is final and cannot be withdrawn.

Category: Academic Procedures
Topic: Procedure for Scrutiny of Evaluation and Grievance Redressal
Applicability: All students wishing to scrutinize MSE/ESE evaluation

Official Procedure:
1. Students are provided an opportunity to inspect evaluated answer sheets after MSE/ESE.
2. Retotalling and rechecking of only unchecked answers, if any, is permitted.
3. Re-evaluation of already checked answers is NOT permissible.
4. In case of grievance related to evaluation, submit a formal representation to the Chairperson, Course Co-ordination Committee (CCC).
5. Final grades are updated based on grade boundaries after considering any approved mark changes.

Category: Academic Procedures
Topic: Procedure for Semester Withdrawal on Medical Grounds
Applicability: Students unable to attend classes due to severe illness or genuine grounds

Official Procedure:
1. Student must submit application for semester withdrawal to Dean Academics through HoD before End Semester Examination.
2. Medical justification must be endorsed by the University Medical Board / Medical Officer.
3. If approved, student is awarded grade 'W' (Withdrawal) for all courses of that semester.
4. Withdrawn semester counts towards the maximum programme duration limit of seven (7) years.
5. Student must re-register for the withdrawn semester in the subsequent academic year.
